key_insight: This paper extends social laws from deterministic multi-agent systems to stochastic, reward-based environments, giving a formal way to design coordination rules that remain effective under uncertainty. It introduces α-robustness to quantify how well a social law protects individual agent performance when conditions vary.
problem_solved: How can we coordinate multiple agents in uncertain, stochastic environments so they avoid interfering with each other and still perform reliably, even when outcomes are reward-based rather than goal-based?
method: Defines social laws for stochastic multi-agent settings instead of only deterministic ones.
Introduces α-robustness as a formal measure of how resilient a social law is to uncertainty and changing conditions.
Provides a verification framework to evaluate whether a proposed social law is robust enough for safe coordination.
impact: This gives AI/ML practitioners a principled way to build more reliable multi-agent systems in realistic environments where randomness and partial unpredictability are unavoidable. It can help improve safety, stability, and performance in coordination-heavy applications such as robotics, traffic, and distributed decision-making.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram comparing deterministic social laws vs. stochastic social laws
Flowchart showing agents -> social law -> reduced interference -> stable rewards
Gauge or meter illustrating α-robustness levels
Icon set for uncertainty, coordination, and reward optimization
paper_title: Social Laws for Multi-agent Coordination in Stochastic Environments
paper_authors: Rolando Fernandez, Caleb Probine, Tyler Lee, Jeffrey Chen, Erez Karpas
